name: Should I add a pantry, island, or bump-out first?

mainEntity.name: Should I add a pantry, island, or bump-out first?
mainEntity.text: Should I add a pantry, island, or bump-out first?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best choice depends on the specific problem in the kitchen. A pantry is usually the right first move when storage is the main issue. An island works best when there is enough room for circulation and the goal is more prep area, seating, or a casual gathering spot. A bump-out is the strongest choice when the kitchen simply does not have enough square footage to function properly. In many Los Angeles homes, the right answer is not the flashiest one but the one that resolves the real bottleneck. Homeowners should measure clearances, traffic paths, and appliance door swings before deciding. A larger space is not always better if it creates awkward dead zones. This is a useful unanswered question because people often ask about features in isolation when they should be prioritizing the layout problem first. Strong content would compare the three options by function, cost, and impact on resale.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose the option that fixes the biggest problem in the kitchen. A pantry adds storage, an island adds prep and seating space, and a bump-out adds square footage. If circulation is tight, a bump-out may help most. If storage is the issue, a pantry may be the best first investment.
